title: Regiment and Uniform
premise: In 1899, on a storm-battered northern coast, Sable Nakamura keeps the Widow's Rock lighthouse alone, hiding her late husband's Japanese name behind a widow's black and a keeper's routine. When a half-drowned stranger washes ashore carrying a letter in the unmistakable hand of Elias Vane — a man officially executed two years ago — Sable learns the 'corpse' was framed by a coastal smuggling ring that includes the magistrate who signed his death warrant. The letter is Vane's confession and the ledger proving it, and it must reach a traveling assize judge before the circuit leaves in eleven days. Smuggling the evidence past three checkpoints, Sable and the stranger, Vane's daughter in disguise, are hunted by the magistrate's men through the great storms; at the climax Sable uses the lighthouse itself — its light, its fog signal, its treacherous rocks — to trap the ring and deliver the ledger, trading her anonymity and her keeper's post for justice. The novel ends with the magistrate arrested, Vane pardoned posthumously, and Sable lighting the lamp one last time before handing over the keys, no longer hiding.
about_author: Astrid Sandoval is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logbooks and assize records from the North Atlantic coast. Regiment and Uniform is her third novel, drawing on real cases of posthumous pardons and the forgotten women who kept remote lights burning.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Opening the 1899 storm season at Widow's Rock, Sable polishes the great lens, counts supplies, and buries grief in routine. A supply boat skips its run — the first missed delivery in years. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: What the Sea Gives Back
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. After a night of violent surf, Sable finds a half-drowned stranger tangled in the rocks below the tower — a young woman clutching an oilskin packet. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding caution.

chapters.title: The Handwriting of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The stranger, calling herself 'Ruth,' recovers by the stove. Sable discovers the packet holds a letter in the handwriting of Elias Vane, hanged two winters past — the man whose trial Sable's late husband attended. Emotional beat: dread blooming in a quiet kitchen.

chapters.title: Ruth, Who Lies Badly
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth deflects questions with thin lies; we learn she is Vane's daughter, come to retrieve the confession her father smuggled out before his execution. Emotional beat: guilt and fear of trusting a stranger.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Warrant
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The letter names Magistrate Corliss Hobb as the man who framed Vane to protect a smuggling ring moving contraband through three coastal checkpoints. The ledger lists bribes, dates, signatures — including Hobb's. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of knowing too much.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The assize judge, Justice Merrow, arrives at the county seat in eleven days and leaves on the mail packet — the only authority outside Hobb's reach. They must move the evidence through three checkpoints. Emotional beat: a plan forming out of desperation.

chapters.title: The Logbook Habit
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable logs the wreck and the survivor honestly, then burns her draft — a keeper's first falsified entry, a small treason. Emotional beat: the cost of the first compromise.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Disguised as sisters traveling to a funeral, they pass the toll bridge, where a bored customs officer almost finds the ledger sewn into Sable's mourning skirt. Emotional beat: terror disguised as grief.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Her Husband
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the market town, an old fisherman recognizes Sable's surname and speaks of Kenji Nakamura kindly — the first person in years to say her husband's name aloud. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into memory.

chapters.title: Hobb's Men
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Two riders in magistrate's livery begin asking after two women on the coast road. Ruth realizes the ring has a description of her from the wreck site. Emotional beat: the hunt tightening.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Church
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sheltering from a storm in a cliff chapel, they discover the ring's drop point — contraband hidden beneath the floor, and fresh boot prints meaning someone is expected tonight. Emotional beat: stumbling into the enemy's heart.

chapters.title: The Night Watcher
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. They hide and watch a handoff: the customs sergeant from the toll bridge is on the ring's payroll. They now know which of the three checkpoints is rotten — and which two merely dangerous. Emotional beat: knowledge as both weapon and burden.

chapters.title: A Debt in Salt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable calls in an old favor from a retired keeper, Marta Quill, who owes Kenji his life. Marta agrees to hide them and the ledger — but warns that Hobb has offered a reward for 'the Vane girl.' Emotional beat: the fragile arithmetic of loyalty.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Ferry at Gray Mouth
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. At the river ferry, the crossing is suspended for the storm; they must bribe a ferryman or wait for Hobb's riders to arrive. Sable trades her wedding ring for a night crossing. Emotional beat: sacrifice made without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Middle of the Water
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Mid-crossing, the ferry is hailed by a patrol boat. The ferryman kills his lamp and drifts; the ledger sits against Sable's heart while oars are muffled. Emotional beat: held breath, shared silence.

chapters.title: What Kenji Taught Me
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Waiting out the storm in Marta's cottage, Sable tells the story of her husband — how he came to the coast, how the town's suspicion outlived him, why she hides his name. Emotional beat: the theme of belonging made explicit.

chapters.title: The Reward Poster
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. A poster in a village window: 'WANTED — RUTH VANE, ACCESSORY TO TREASON, 50 POUNDS.' Her father's crime has been rewritten onto her. Emotional beat: fury sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They learn the informant who betrayed Vane originally was his own clerk, now Hobb's chief man, Sergeant Aldous Pike. Pike is stationed at checkpoint three. Emotional beat: the enemy acquires a face.

chapters.title: Marta's Price
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Marta's son is a customs rider; helping them could hang him. Marta asks them to leave before he returns. They go at dawn into worsening weather. Emotional beat: kindness with a limit, honored without bitterness.

chapters.title: The Storm Season Turns
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The great storm of the year arrives early; roads flood, the mail packet may not sail, and the judge's departure date is suddenly uncertain — both threat and opportunity. Emotional beat: nature indifferent to their deadline.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Pike Gate
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The final checkpoint is a fortified customs house commanded by Pike himself. Direct passage is impossible; they must go over the headland — through the flooded quarry — or find a way to make Pike open his own gate. Emotional beat: the wall that must become a door.

chapters.title: The Quarry Flood
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Crossing the flooded quarry at night, Ruth is nearly swept away; Sable goes in after her, and they survive on a ledge until dawn, the ledger soaked but legible. Emotional beat: the stranger becomes a sister.

chapters.title: Drying the Truth
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. They dry each ledger page by a peat fire, reading every entry — learning the ring's full shape: magistrates, sergeants, a shipping magnate, and a name that makes Sable go still. Emotional beat: intimacy forged by shared evidence.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. One ledger margin lists a payment to a 'K. Nakamura, keeper' — a bribe her husband never took, recorded to bind him in silence. Sable finally understands why Kenji died in that 'accident.' Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Plan of the Light
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Sable proposes the impossible: use the lighthouse. Its lamp, fog signal, and the rocks it guards can stop Hobb's pursuit and signal the assize judge's escort ship. But it means going back to Widow's Rock, where they'll be expected. Emotional beat: turning her refuge into a weapon.

chapters.title: Pike's Letter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They intercept a message from Pike to Hobb: the 'Vane girl' was seen heading for the coast; seal the roads and search every keeper's station. The trap is being set for them — and Sable decides to walk into it. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Long Road Home
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The journey back along the drowned coast road, past checkpoints now hunting them, past the toll bridge sergeant who looks at Sable one beat too long. Emotional beat: dread measured in footsteps.

chapters.title: The Empty Tower
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They reach Widow's Rock and find the lighthouse door forced, the lamp room searched — but the oil untouched. Hobb's men are waiting nearby, not inside. Sable begins her preparations: mirrors, oil, the fog signal's steam valve. Emotional beat: a keeper reclaiming her ground.

chapters.title: The Judge's Ship
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Offshore, Justice Merrow's escort ship rides at anchor, delayed by the storm, waiting for the channel to be confirmed safe. One signal from the light could bring it in — or the rocks could wreck it. Emotional beat: hope balanced on a knife's edge of risk.

chapters.title: Hobb Comes to the Light
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Magistrate Hobb arrives personally, with Pike and six men, to search the tower and arrest 'the widow.' Sable greets him at the door with tea and a keeper's courtesy, stalling while Ruth climbs toward the lamp room. Emotional beat: courtesy as combat.

chapters.title: The Stairwell
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth hides in the lamp room as Pike climbs to inspect it; she overhears Hobb and Pike below admit Kenji's murder in so many words. Emotional beat: horror and vindication in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Lamp Is Lit
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At full dark, in the teeth of the great storm, Sable lights the lamp and turns the lens not to the safe channel but to the wreck-stones — a keeper's signal that something is wrong, the old code every captain knows. Emotional beat: defiance made of light.

chapters.title: The Fog Signal
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth opens the steam valve; the fog signal screams a distress pattern over the storm. Hobb's men rush the tower. The escort ship answers: rockets go up offshore, and a boarding party puts out through the swell. Emotional beat: the world finally hearing them.

chapters.title: The Rocks Do Their Work
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hobb's pursuit boat, chasing the judge's launch in the dark Sable's signal has confused, strikes the Widow's Rock shoal. Hobb survives; his evidence-men and their contraband do not. Emotional beat: terrible justice, no triumph in it.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. In the lamp room, by the rotating light, Ruth reads the ledger aloud to Justice Merrow while Hobb, soaked and cuffed, listens to his own signature condemned. Pike turns crown's evidence. Emotional beat: the dead man's hand speaking at last.

chapters.title: The Assize at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A makeshift hearing in the harbor customs hall; witnesses, the fisherman, Marta, the ferryman. Hobb is committed for trial; Vane's conviction is quashed and a posthumous pardon entered. Emotional beat: justice arriving plain and unglamorous, and enough.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth, cleared of the false warrant, asks Sable to come south with her — a home, a family of sorts. Sable looks at the tower she must soon surrender. Emotional beat: the choice between safety and self.

chapters.title: The Last Watch
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The new keeper arrives; Sable walks him through the routines, corrects his trim of the wick, and writes her final honest logbook entry — including her full name, Kenji's name, and the truth of the storm. Emotional beat: putting down the armor.

chapters.title: Regiment and Uniform
chapters.summary: Sable and Ruth's alternating POV. On the mail packet's deck, Sable watches Widow's Rock's light flare for the first watch under new hands. She wears no mourning now, no disguise, no borrowed name. Emotional beat: belonging finally worn openly, like a uniform she chose.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV, epilogue. A year later, Ruth publishes her father's vindicated letters; a package arrives at their door containing Sable's old logbook and a note: the new keeper asks her to inspect his work. Sable smiles, packs her oilskins. Emotional beat: the light passed on, the story closed but still burning.
